_meta.title: Surah An-Naba (78)
_meta.description: Surah An-Naba, The Great News: phrase meanings, tafsir and Arabic vocabulary.

q1.question: What is the English meaning for the surah's title, An-Naba, النَّبَإِ?
q1.explanation: النَّبَإِ (An-Naba) means 'The Great News' or 'The Tidings,' derived from the root ن-ب-أ, referring to the momentous news of the Day of Resurrection.

q2.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ' mean?
options: What are they asking one another about?
q2.explanation: عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ ('Amma yatasaa'alun) means 'What are they asking one another about?' root س-أ-ل (ask/question).

q3.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ' mean?
q3.explanation: عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ ('Ani an-naba'i al-'azim) means 'About the great news,' roots ن-ب-أ (news) and ع-ظ-م (great).

q4.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ' mean?
options: That about which they are in disagreement
That about which they are in agreement
That about which they are certain
That about which they are united
q4.explanation: الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ (Alladhi hum fihi mukhtalifun) means 'That about which they are in disagreement,' root خ-ل-ف (differ/disagree).

q5.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ' mean?
options: No! They are going to know
q5.explanation: كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ (Kalla saya'lamun) means 'No! They are going to know,' root ع-ل-م (know), expressing certainty about future knowledge.

q6.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا' mean?
options: Have We not made the earth unstable?
Have We not made the earth spherical?
Have We not made the earth motionless?
Have We not made the earth a resting place?
q6.explanation: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا (Alam naj'ali al-arda mihada) means 'Have We not made the earth a resting place?' roots ج-ع-ل (make), أ-ر-ض (earth), م-ه-د (cradle/resting place).

q7.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا' mean?
q7.explanation: وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا (Wal-jibala awtada) means 'And the mountains as stakes,' roots ج-ب-ل (mountains) and و-ت-د (pegs/stakes).

q8.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا' mean?
options: And We created you in pairs
q8.explanation: وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا (Wa khalaqnakum azwaja) means 'And We created you in pairs,' roots خ-ل-ق (create) and ز-و-ج (pairs/spouses).

q9.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا' mean?
options: And We made your sleep an activity
And We made your sleep a punishment
And We made your sleep rest
And We made your sleep a burden
q9.explanation: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا (Wa ja'alna nawmakum subata) means 'And We made your sleep rest,' roots ج-ع-ل (make), ن-و-م (sleep), س-ب-ت (rest/repose).

q10.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا' mean?
options: And We made the night bright
And We made the night covering
And We made the night short
And We made the night warm
q10.explanation: وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا (Wa ja'alna al-layla libasa) means 'And We made the night covering,' roots ج-ع-ل (make), ل-ي-ل (night), ل-ب-س (covering/garment).

q11.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا' mean?
options: And We made the day for livelihood
And We made the day for sleep
And We made the day for rest
And We made the day for darkness
q11.explanation: وَجَعَلْنَا النَّهَارَ مَعَاشًا (Wa ja'alna an-nahara ma'asha) means 'And We made the day for livelihood,' roots ج-ع-ل (make), ن-ه-ر (day), ع-ي-ش (livelihood).

q12.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا' mean?
options: And We constructed beneath you seven weak layers
And We constructed above you seven strong
And We constructed beside you seven fragile
And We constructed within you seven soft
q12.explanation: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًا شِدَادًا (Wa banayna fawqakum sab'an shidada) means 'And We constructed above you seven strong [heavens],' roots ب-ن-ي (build), س-ب-ع (seven), ش-د-د (strong).

q13.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا' mean?
options: And We made a burning lamp
And We made a dim light
And We made a cold star
And We made a hidden moon
q13.explanation: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا (Wa ja'alna sirajan wahhaja) means 'And We made a burning lamp,' roots ج-ع-ل (make), س-ر-ج (lamp), و-ه-ج (blazing/burning).

q14.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا' mean?
options: And We sent down from the clouds a little water
And We sent down from the mountains dry dust
And We sent down from the rainclouds pouring water
And We sent down from the sky frozen ice
q14.explanation: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ الْمُعْصِرَاتِ مَاءً ثَجَّاجًا (Wa anzalna mina al-mu'sirati ma'an thajjaja) means 'And We sent down from the rainclouds pouring water,' roots ن-ز-ل (send down), ع-ص-ر (squeeze/clouds), م-و-ء (water), ث-ج-ج (pouring).

q15.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا' mean?
options: That We may destroy grain and plants
That We may hide grain and plants
That We may forget grain and plants
That We may bring forth thereby grain and plants
q15.explanation: لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَبَاتًا (Linukhrija bihi habban wanabata) means 'That We may bring forth thereby grain and plants,' roots خ-ر-ج (bring forth), ح-ب-ب (grain), ن-ب-ت (plants).

q16.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا' mean?
q16.explanation: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفَافًا (Wa jannatin alfafa) means 'And gardens of dense greenery,' roots ج-ن-ن (gardens) and ل-ف-ف (intertwined/dense).

q17.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتًا' mean?
options: Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time
Indeed, the Day of Decision is uncertain
Indeed, the Day of Decision is forgotten
Indeed, the Day of Decision is cancelled
q17.explanation: إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَاتًا (Inna yawma al-fasli kana miqata) means 'Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time,' roots ي-و-م (day), ف-ص-ل (decision/separation), و-ق-ت (appointed time).

q18.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا' mean?
options: The Day the Horn is blown and you come individually
The Day the Horn is blown and you come in companies
The Day the Horn is blown and you come willingly
The Day the Horn is blown and you come unknowingly
q18.explanation: 'يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا'  (Yawma unfahu fisuri fatau thuna afwaja) means 'The Day the Horn is blown and you come in companies,' roots ي-و-م (day), ف-ص-ل (decision/separation), و-ق-ت (appointed time).

q19.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَفُتِحَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا' mean?
options: And the heaven is closed and becomes sealed
And the heaven is hidden and becomes dark
And the heaven is opened and becomes gateways
And the heaven is covered and becomes solid
q19.explanation: وَفُتِحَتِ السَّمَاءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَابًا (Wa futihati as-sama'u fakanat abwaba) means 'And the heaven is opened and becomes gateways,' roots ف-ت-ح (open), س-م-و (heaven), ب-و-ب (doors/gateways).

q20.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا' mean?
options: And the mountains are made firm and become solid
And the mountains are removed and become a mirage
And the mountains are raised and become tall
And the mountains are planted and become green
q20.explanation: وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا (Wa suyyirati al-jibalu fakanat saraba) means 'And the mountains are removed and become a mirage,' roots س-ي-ر (move/set in motion), ج-ب-ل (mountains), س-ر-ب (mirage).

q21.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا' mean?
options: Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait
q21.explanation: إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا (Inna jahannama kanat mirsada) means 'Indeed, Hell has been lying in wait,' roots ج-ه-ن-م (Hell/Gehenna) and ر-ص-د (lying in wait/ambush).

q22.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'لِّلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا' mean?
options: For the transgressors a place of return
q22.explanation: لِّلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا (Littaghina ma'aba) means 'For the transgressors a place of return,' roots ط-غ-و (transgress) and أ-و-ب (return/resort).

q23.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'لَابِثِينَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا' mean?
options: In which they will remain for ages
In which they will remain for moments
In which they will remain for days
In which they will remain for hours
q23.explanation: لَابِثِينَ فِيهَا أَحْقَابًا (Labithina fiha ahqaba) means 'In which they will remain for ages,' roots ل-ب-ث (remain/stay) and ح-ق-ب (ages/long periods).

q24.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا وَلَا شَرَابًا' mean?
options: They will taste therein warmth and food
They will taste therein comfort and pleasure
They will not taste therein coolness or drink
They will taste therein sweetness and nectar
q24.explanation: لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًا وَلَا شَرَابًا (La yadhquqna fiha bardan wala sharaba) means 'They will not taste therein coolness or drink,' roots ذ-و-ق (taste), ب-ر-د (coolness), ش-ر-ب (drink).

q25.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا' mean?
options: Except scalding water and purulent fluid
q25.explanation: إِلَّا حَمِيمًا وَغَسَّاقًا (Illa hamiman waghassaqa) means 'Except scalding water and purulent fluid,' roots ح-م-م (scalding/hot) and غ-س-ق (purulent/discharge).

q26.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا' mean?
q26.explanation: جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا (Jaza'an wifaqa) means 'An appropriate recompense,' roots ج-ز-ي (recompense) and و-ف-ق (fitting/appropriate).

q27.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًا' mean?
options: Indeed, they were not expecting an account
Indeed, they were expecting a reward
Indeed, they were hoping for mercy
q27.explanation: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًا (Innahum kanu la yarjuna hisaba) means 'Indeed, they were not expecting an account,' roots ك-و-ن (were), ر-ج-و (expect/hope), ح-س-ب (account/reckoning).

q28.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّابًا' mean?
options: And they believed in Our verses completely
And they denied Our verses with denial
And they accepted Our verses with acceptance
And they pondered Our verses with thought
q28.explanation: وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا كِذَّابًا (Wa kadhhabu bi'ayatina kidhdhaba) means 'And they denied Our verses with denial,' roots ك-ذ-ب (deny/lie) and آ-ي-ت (verses/signs).

q29.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَابًا' mean?
options: And all things We have enumerated in writing
And all things We have hidden away
And all things We have destroyed completely
And all things We have forgotten entirely
q29.explanation: وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ كِتَابًا (Wa kulla shay'in ahsaynahu kitaba) means 'And all things We have enumerated in writing,' roots ش-ي-ء (thing), ح-ص-ي (enumerate/count), ك-ت-ب (writing/book).

q30.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا' mean?
options: Indeed, for the sinners is loss
Indeed, for the righteous is success
Indeed, for the wicked is failure
Indeed, for the disbelievers is punishment
q30.explanation: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا (Inna lilmuttaqina mafaza) means 'Indeed, for the righteous is success,' roots ت-ق-ي (be righteous/God-fearing) and ف-و-ز (success/attainment).

q31.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'حَدَائِقَ وَأَعْنَابًا' mean?
q31.explanation: حَدَائِقَ وَأَعْنَابًا (Hada'iqa wa a'naba) means 'Gardens and grapevines,' roots ح-د-ق (gardens) and ع-ن-ب (grapes/grapevines).

q32.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَابًا' mean?
options: And old women of different ages
And young men of various sizes
q32.explanation: وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَابًا (Wa kawa'iba atraba) means 'And companions of equal age,' roots ك-ع-ب (full-breasted/youthful) and ت-ر-ب (of equal age).

q33.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا' mean?
q33.explanation: وَكَأْسًا دِهَاقًا (Wa ka'san dihaqa) means 'And a full cup,' roots ك-أ-س (cup) and د-ه-ق (full/overflowing).

q34.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا وَلَا كِذَّابًا' mean?
options: They will hear therein gossip and lies
They will not hear therein ill speech or falsehood
They will hear therein music and singing
They will hear therein arguments and debates
q34.explanation: لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا وَلَا كِذَّابًا (La yasma'una fiha laghwan wala kidhdhaba) means 'They will not hear therein ill speech or falsehood,' roots س-م-ع (hear), ل-غ-و (vain/idle talk), ك-ذ-ب (falsehood).

q35.question: What does the Arabic phrase 'جَزَاءً مِّن رَّبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا' mean?
options: [As] punishment from your Lord, a meager withholding
[As] trial from your Lord, a difficult test
[As] warning from your Lord, a stern reminder
[As] reward from your Lord, a calculated gift
q35.explanation: جَزَاءً مِّن رَّبِّكَ عَطَاءً حِسَابًا (Jaza'an min rabbika 'ata'an hisaba) means '[As] reward from your Lord, a calculated gift,' roots ج-ز-ي (reward), ر-ب-ب (Lord), ع-ط-و (gift/bestowal), ح-س-ب (calculated/sufficient).

q36.question: According to the opening verses, what is the 'great news' chiefly about?
options: The coming of the Day of Resurrection
The appointment of the first caliph
q36.explanation: The opening passage concerns the momentous news of resurrection and the Hereafter. Classical tafsir identifies this as the central subject of the dispute. (78:1–5; Tafsir al-Tabari on 78:1)

q37.question: What historical setting is traditionally assigned to Surah An-Naba?
options: A Madinan surah revealed after Badr
A Makkan surah from the early preaching period
A surah revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage
q37.explanation: The surah is classified as Makkan. Its emphasis on resurrection, accountability, and the signs of divine power fits the central themes of the Makkan period. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir, introduction to Surah 78)

q38.question: What does the opening question 'عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ' convey in its context?
options: A question exposing people's discussion and dispute over the great news
A question about the direction of prayer
q38.explanation: The opening draws attention to what the people were discussing and disputing: the great news, understood by the commentators as resurrection and judgement. (78:1–3; al-Tabari)

q39.question: Why does the surah repeat 'كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ' and then 'ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ'?
options: To indicate uncertainty about the Hereafter
To deny that judgement will occur
To mark two different creation stories
To intensify the warning that they will soon know the truth
q39.explanation: The repeated warning emphatically rejects their denial and stresses the certainty of the reality they will encounter. (78:4–5; Ibn Kathir)

q40.question: How do verses 6–16 support the argument for resurrection?
options: They cite creation and recurring blessings as signs of Allah's power
They describe the genealogy of the Quraysh
They give a timetable for the Last Day
q40.explanation: The earth, mountains, human pairs, sleep, night, day, heavens, sun, rain and vegetation are presented as signs of the Creator's power and wisdom. The One who created these can resurrect people. (78:6–16; Maududi, Tafhim al-Qur'an)

q41.question: What is the significance of describing the earth as 'مِهَادًا'?
options: It means the earth is a temporary illusion
It portrays the earth as a prepared resting place or cradle
It means the earth is made of iron
It refers only to the mountains
q41.explanation: Mihād conveys a spread-out or prepared resting place. The verse invites reflection on the earth as a provision made suitable for human life. (78:6; Qur'an 78:6)

q42.question: In verse 7, mountains are described as 'أَوْتَادًا' (stakes). What is the image conveyed?
options: Mountains are buildings constructed by people
Mountains are signs of the coming rain only
The image compares mountains to pegs or stakes
q42.explanation: Awtād is the plural of watad, a peg or stake. The verse uses this image in describing the mountains as part of Allah's ordered creation. (78:7; Ibn Kathir)

q43.question: What does the pairing 'وَخَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا' most directly affirm?
options: Allah created human beings in pairs
q43.explanation: The verse points to Allah's creation of human beings as pairs. The wording is part of the sequence of blessings and signs in verses 6–16. (78:8)

q44.question: What does 'وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًا' teach about sleep?
options: Sleep is a divinely provided period of rest and cessation
Sleep is a punishment for every person
Sleep is forbidden during the night
q44.explanation: Subāt conveys rest, cessation, or relief from activity. Sleep is presented as one of Allah's mercies and signs. (78:9; Ibn Kathir)

q45.question: How do verses 10–11 describe the complementary functions of night and day?
options: Both are intended only for sleep
Night is a covering, while day is made for livelihood
Night is for trade and day for burial
Both are described as permanent darkness
q45.explanation: Night is likened to a garment or covering, while daylight is made a means for livelihood and activity. (78:10–11)

q46.question: What is the function of the sun in the description 'سِرَاجًا وَهَّاجًا'?
options: A lamp that gives no heat or light
A star that appears only at night
q46.explanation: Sirāj wahhāj depicts a brightly blazing lamp, commonly understood in the verse as the sun. It is another sign of Allah's creative power. (78:13; Ibn Kathir)

q47.question: What is the sequence described in verses 14–16?
options: The sea dries up and mountains become gardens
The stars fall and the earth becomes dark
Rain is sent down, bringing forth grain, plants and dense gardens
q47.explanation: The passage describes abundant rain followed by the growth of grain, vegetation and lush gardens. It is an example of provision and a sign of divine power. (78:14–16)

q48.question: What does 'يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ' mean in the context of verse 17?
options: The Day of Decision and separation
q48.explanation: Yawm al-Faṣl is the Day of Decision, when judgement separates people according to their deeds. (78:17; Ibn Kathir)

q49.question: What does 'فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًا' indicate?
options: People will remain in their graves
Only one nation will be resurrected
People will come forth in groups
People will enter the world again as infants
q49.explanation: Afwājan means groups or companies. The verse describes people coming in groups after the Trumpet is blown. (78:18)

q50.question: What happens to the mountains in verse 20?
options: They are set in motion and become like a mirage
q50.explanation: The surah describes the mountains being moved until they appear like a mirage. This is part of the cosmic upheaval of the Last Day. (78:20; compare 20:105–107)

q51.question: How is Hell described in verse 21?
options: As a place lying in wait
As a temporary resting place for everyone
As a place that no one will approach
q51.explanation: Mirṣād means a place of watch or ambush, conveying that Hell awaits those destined for it. (78:21; Ibn Kathir)

q52.question: Who are the people described as 'لِّلطَّاغِينَ مَآبًا'?
options: The transgressors, for whom it is a place of return
q52.explanation: Ṭāghīn refers to those who transgress the bounds. The passage describes Hell as their destination. (78:22)

q53.question: What does 'أَحْقَابًا' in verse 23 mean?
q53.explanation: Aḥqāb is the plural of ḥuqb, referring to long periods or ages. The verse describes the duration of the punishment in the passage. (78:23; consult classical tafsir for the detailed discussion)

q54.question: What is the contrast in verses 24–25?
options: They will find no coolness or drink except scalding water and ghassaq
q54.explanation: The passage depicts the punishment of the people of Hell: they will not taste coolness or drink, except what is specified in verse 25. (78:24–25)

q55.question: What does 'جَزَاءً وِفَاقًا' emphasise?
options: A recompense corresponding to what was earned
A reward given without any relation to deeds
q55.explanation: The phrase means a fitting or corresponding recompense. The context links the punishment to the people's deeds and denial. (78:26–28)

q56.question: According to verse 27, what attitude contributed to the transgressors' fate?
options: They regularly expected the final account
They did not expect an accounting
They were unaware of ordinary daily events
They had forgotten their family names
q56.explanation: The verse says they did not expect a reckoning. The following verse mentions their denial of Allah's signs. (78:27–28)

q57.question: What does verse 29 say about the recording of deeds?
options: Deeds are recorded only after death by relatives
Everything has been enumerated and recorded
q57.explanation: The verse states that every thing has been enumerated in a record. This accords with other Qur'anic passages affirming the recording and preservation of deeds. (78:29; compare 18:49)

q58.question: What is the force of the command 'فَذُوقُوا' in verse 30?
options: An invitation to taste a garden fruit
A rebuke announcing the consequence of their deeds
q58.explanation: In context, 'Taste!' is a stern address to those receiving punishment. The verse continues by saying that they will be given no increase except in punishment. (78:30)

q59.question: What major contrast begins at verse 31?
options: The passage turns from Hell's punishment to the success prepared for the mindful
The passage returns to the creation of mountains
The passage begins a story about a prophet
The passage changes to laws of pilgrimage
q59.explanation: Verse 31 begins the contrasting description of the success and reward of the muttaqīn after the preceding description of Hell. (78:31–36)

q60.question: Who are 'الْمُتَّقِينَ' in the context of this surah?
options: Those mindful of Allah who guard themselves against disobedience
Those who live only in the desert
q60.explanation: Al-Muttaqīn refers to people of taqwā: those mindful of Allah and seeking to obey Him. The surah describes their reward in verses 31–36. (78:31)

q61.question: Which items are explicitly mentioned among the delights of Paradise in verses 32–34?
options: Gardens, grapevines and a full cup
q61.explanation: The verses mention gardens, grapevines, companions of equal age, and a cup filled abundantly. (78:32–34)

q62.question: What does verse 35 say will be absent from the gathering in Paradise?
q62.explanation: The people of Paradise will not hear vain or false speech there. This highlights the purity and peace of the final abode. (78:35)

q63.question: What does 'عَطَاءً حِسَابًا' in verse 36 convey?
options: A generous, sufficient gift from the Lord
A loan that must be repaid
A gift from one human ruler
A reward whose amount is unknown to Allah
q63.explanation: The phrase describes the reward as a gift from the Lord, abundant and sufficient. Tafsir explains the expression in the context of the reward of the people of taqwā. (78:36; Ibn Kathir)

q64.question: What does verse 37 emphasise about Allah?
options: He is limited to the heavens
He is the Lord of the heavens, the earth and all between them, the Most Merciful
He shares authority with the angels
q64.explanation: The verse declares Allah's lordship over the heavens, earth and everything between them, and names Him al-Raḥmān. (78:37)

q65.question: Why do the Spirit and angels stand in rows in verse 38?
options: To decide who will create the universe
In awe and obedience before the Most Merciful on the Day of Standing
To prevent people from entering Paradise
q65.explanation: The verse describes the Spirit and angels standing in rows; none speaks except one permitted by the Most Merciful who says what is right. (78:38)

q66.question: What condition is attached to speaking on that Day in verse 38?
options: Anyone may speak whenever they wish
Every person must speak at once
Permission from the Most Merciful, and speaking rightly
q66.explanation: The verse restricts speech to one whom the Most Merciful permits and who speaks correctly. (78:38)

q67.question: What does verse 39 call the Day of Judgement?
options: A day that may never occur
q67.explanation: Dhālika al-yawm al-ḥaqq means 'That is the True Day.' The surah concludes by affirming its certainty and urging people to take a return to their Lord. (78:39)

q68.question: What choice is presented in 'فَمَن شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ مَآبًا'?
options: People may choose whether Allah exists
Whoever wills may take a path of return to their Lord
People can choose to cancel the Day of Judgement
Only angels can return to Allah
q68.explanation: The verse calls people to take a way of return to their Lord. Human choice and responsibility are emphasised, while the surrounding verses warn of the coming reality. (78:39)

q69.question: What is the 'near punishment' mentioned in verse 40?
options: A punishment that occurred only in ancient times
The punishment of the Hereafter, near in the certainty of its arrival
A punishment that affects only one tribe
q69.explanation: The warning calls the punishment 'near' because the Hereafter is certain and approaching, not because its timing is disclosed to people. (78:40; compare 70:6–7)

q70.question: Which authentic/hasan report specifically names 'عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ' among the surahs that deeply affected the Prophet ﷺ?
options: The report in Jamiʿ al-Tirmidhi 3297, in which he says that Hud, al-Waqiʿah, al-Mursalat, An-Naba and at-Takwir made his hair turn grey
A report that An-Naba was revealed during the Battle of Badr
A report that An-Naba was the last surah revealed
A report that An-Naba was recited only at weddings
q70.explanation: In Jamiʿ al-Tirmidhi 3297, Abu Bakr asks the Prophet ﷺ about his greying hair; the Prophet names Hud, al-Waqiʿah, al-Mursalat, 'Amma yatasa'alun (An-Naba), and at-Takwir. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan gharīb; Darussalam grades it sahih. The report highlights the weight of the warnings and descriptions of the Hereafter. (Jamiʿ al-Tirmidhi 3297)

q71.question: In verse 1, what is the grammatical and lexical sense of 'يَتَسَاءَلُونَ'?
q71.explanation: Yatasā'alūn is a Form VI imperfect verb from س-أ-ل, conveying reciprocal asking or questioning. (78:1)

q72.question: The word 'النَّبَإِ' is derived from which root and means what?
q72.explanation: Al-naba' comes from ن-ب-أ and means news or tidings, especially momentous news in this context. (78:2)

q73.question: What does the adjective 'الْعَظِيمِ' mean?
q73.explanation: Al-ʿaẓīm is from ع-ظ-م and means great, tremendous or mighty. It describes the momentous news. (78:2)

q74.question: What is the meaning of 'مُخْتَلِفُونَ' in verse 3?
q74.explanation: Mukhtalifūn is the active participle plural from خ-ل-ف, here meaning those who differ or disagree. (78:3)

q75.question: What does the emphatic particle 'كَلَّا' communicate here?
options: No indeed; a strong rejection or rebuke
q75.explanation: Kallā is a particle used here to reject the denial and introduce a stern warning. (78:4)

q76.question: The verb 'سَيَعْلَمُونَ' contains the prefix 'سَـ'. What does it indicate?
q76.explanation: The prefix sa- marks the future. Sayaʿlamūn means 'they will know' or 'they shall soon know.' (78:4)

q77.question: What is the meaning of 'مِهَادًا' in verse 6?
options: A prepared resting place or cradle
q77.explanation: Mihādan comes from م-ه-د and conveys a prepared resting place, cradle or spread-out bed. (78:6)

q78.question: What is the singular form related to 'أَوْتَادًا'?
q78.explanation: Awtād is the plural of watad, meaning a peg or stake. The verse compares mountains to stakes. (78:7)

q79.question: What does 'أَزْوَاجًا' mean in verse 8?
q79.explanation: Azwājan is the plural of zawj and means pairs, mates or spouses, according to context. (78:8)

q80.question: What is the meaning of 'سُبَاتًا'?
q80.explanation: Subātan is associated with the root س-ب-ت and means rest or cessation from activity. (78:9)

q81.question: In verse 10, what does 'لِبَاسًا' mean literally?
q81.explanation: Libāsan means clothing or covering. Night is likened to a garment that covers. (78:10)

q82.question: What does 'مَعَاشًا' mean in verse 11?
options: A means or period of livelihood
q82.explanation: Maʿāshan is related to ع-ي-ش, life or living; it refers to the day as a time for livelihood and activity. (78:11)

q83.question: What is the meaning of 'شِدَادًا' in verse 12?
q83.explanation: Shidādan is the plural form conveying strength or firmness, describing the seven heavens. (78:12)

q84.question: What does 'سِرَاجًا' mean?
q84.explanation: Sirājan means a lamp or source of light. In verse 13 it refers to the blazing sun. (78:13)

q85.question: What is the force of the intensive form 'وَهَّاجًا'?
q85.explanation: Wahhājan is an intensive form from و-ه-ج, conveying intense brightness, blazing heat or radiance. (78:13)

q86.question: What does 'الْمُعْصِرَاتِ' refer to in the verse?
options: Rain-bearing clouds (as explained by many commentators)
q86.explanation: Al-muʿṣirāt is interpreted by many commentators as clouds from which rain is pressed or sent down; tafsir records linguistic and interpretive discussion. (78:14)

q87.question: What does 'ثَجَّاجًا' describe?
q87.explanation: Thajjājan, from ث-ج-ج, describes water pouring forth abundantly. (78:14)

q88.question: What does 'حَبًّا' mean in verse 15?
q88.explanation: Ḥabban refers to grain or seeds, brought forth by the rain. (78:15)

q89.question: What is the meaning of 'نَبَاتًا'?
q89.explanation: Nabātan means plant growth or vegetation, from the root ن-ب-ت. (78:15)

q90.question: What does 'أَلْفَافًا' convey about the gardens?
q90.explanation: Alfāfan describes gardens with dense, intertwined growth. It is a rare Qur'anic form in this verse. (78:16)

q91.question: What is the meaning of 'الْفَصْلِ' in 'يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ'?
q91.explanation: Al-faṣl comes from ف-ص-ل and conveys separating, distinguishing or deciding. Yawm al-faṣl is the Day of Decision. (78:17)

q92.question: What does 'مِيقَاتًا' mean?
q92.explanation: Mīqātan is an appointed time or fixed appointment, from the root و-ق-ت. (78:17)

q93.question: What does the passive verb 'يُنفَخُ' mean in verse 18?
q93.explanation: Yunfakhu is a passive imperfect verb from ن-ف-خ, meaning 'it is blown'; the verse refers to the Trumpet. (78:18)

q94.question: What does 'أَفْوَاجًا' mean?
q94.explanation: Afwājan is the plural of fawj, meaning a group, company or multitude. (78:18)

q95.question: What is the meaning of 'أَبْوَابًا' in verse 19?
q95.explanation: Abwāban is the plural of bāb, meaning doors or gates. The heaven is described as becoming gateways. (78:19)

q96.question: What does 'سَرَابًا' mean in verse 20?
q96.explanation: Sarāban means a mirage, an appearance that seems real from a distance. The mountains are described as becoming like one. (78:20)

q97.question: What does 'مِرْصَادًا' convey?
options: A place of watch or ambush; lying in wait
q97.explanation: Mirṣādan is related to ر-ص-د and conveys a place of observation or ambush, hence 'lying in wait.' (78:21)

q98.question: What is the meaning of 'الطَّاغِينَ'?
q98.explanation: Al-ṭāghīn is the plural of ṭāghin, from ط-غ-ي/ط-غ-و, referring to those who transgress or exceed bounds. (78:22)

q99.question: What does 'مَآبًا' mean?
options: A place of return or destination
q99.explanation: Ma'āban comes from أ-و-ب and means a place of return, resort or destination. (78:22)

q100.question: What is the meaning of 'لَابِثِينَ'?
q100.explanation: Lābithīna is an active participle plural from ل-ب-ث, meaning those who remain or stay. (78:23)

q101.question: What does 'أَحْقَابًا' refer to?
q101.explanation: Aḥqāban is the plural of ḥuqb, a long period or age. Commentators discuss its precise scope in this context. (78:23)

q102.question: What does 'حَمِيمًا' mean in verse 25?
q102.explanation: Ḥamīman means intensely hot or scalding water in this context. (78:25)

q103.question: What is the meaning of 'غَسَّاقًا'?
options: A foul, intensely cold or purulent fluid (as explained in tafsir)
q103.explanation: Ghassāqan is a rare word. Classical tafsir gives explanations including foul fluid or intensely cold, noxious liquid; the verse places it among the punishments of Hell. (78:25)

q104.question: What does 'وِفَاقًا' mean in verse 26?
q104.explanation: Wifāqan comes from و-ف-ق and means in accordance, fitting or corresponding. The recompense corresponds to deeds. (78:26)

q105.question: What does 'يَرْجُونَ' mean in verse 27?
q105.explanation: Yarjūna is from ر-ج-و and means they hope for or expect. In context, they did not expect an accounting. (78:27)
